THIS MASTER SERVICE AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is entered into as of {{contract.effectiveDate}} (the “Effective Date”) by and between {{client.legalEntityName}} (the “Client”), located at {{client.address}} and {{onspot.entityName}} (“OnSpot”), {{onspot.entityType}}, located at {{onspot.address}}. Both Client and {{onspot.entityName}} may be referred to in this Agreement individually as a “Party” or collectively as the “Parties.”

NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises contained herein and other good and sufficient consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which is hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereto agree as follows:

1. Services

1.1 Statements of Work. OnSpot agrees to perform the services (the “Services”) for the Client as described in one or more statements of work signed by both Parties in substantially the form attached hereto as Appendix A (each, a “Statement of Work” or “SOW”), the non-exclusivity pertains to the partnership between OnSpot and the Client, according to the terms and conditions outlined in this Agreement. All staff deployed to the Client to perform services outlined in the Statement of Work are exclusive. Under no circumstances will OnSpot deploy the Staff to other clients without the approval of the Client as outlined in Appendix A – Statement of Work, Section 1. Scope of Work.

1.2 Change Orders. In the event either Party requires a material change to a Statement of Work, such Party will provide a written change order to the other for approval, specifying the change required (each a “Change Order”). Each Party agrees that a Change Order will be required. There may be fees incurred depending on the request or change subject to the agreement of both parties. A Change Order must be signed by both Parties to be effective.

1.3 Conflicts & Order of Precedence. In the event of a conflict between the terms and conditions of the main body of this Agreement and those of a Statement of Work or Change Order, the terms and conditions of the main body of this Agreement will control, unless specifically stated otherwise in the Statement of Work or Change Order.

1.4 Client Assistance. The Client shall provide OnSpot with such resources, information and assistance as OnSpot may reasonably request in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement. In the event the Services are provided on Client’s premises, Client shall provide safe and adequate space, power, network connections and such other resources as reasonably requested by OnSpot and OnSpot shall comply with all security, confidentiality, safety and health policies of Client.

1.5 Success Manager. OnSpot will provide the client with access to a shared Success Manager, also known as an Account Manager. This person will act as a liaison between the client and the OnSpot team performing Services. The Account Manager will be available for regular meetings between the Client and the OnSpot team. The Account Manager will help ensure the OnSpot team is meeting the Client’s expectations.

1.6 Client Materials. Client acknowledges that to perform the Services, OnSpot may require access to certain Client software or other information or material from Client or Client’s suppliers (“Client Materials”). Accordingly, Client hereby grants to OnSpot a non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to use the Client Materials solely as necessary for OnSpot to perform the Services for Client.

2. Payment Terms

2.1 Compensation. In consideration of the Services, Client shall pay OnSpot as set forth herein and in the applicable Statement of Work.

2.2 Expenses. Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, each Party will bear its own costs and expenses incurred in connection with the performance of its obligations under this Agreement. No Party shall have any right to any reimbursement, payment or compensation of any kind from the other for such obligations and efforts except as expressly set forth in this Agreement or an applicable Change Order or Statement of Work.

2.3 Security Deposit. Client shall provide a security deposit equal to one (1) month's total invoice amount prior to the Program Launch Date and before any Services commence. This deposit is a condition precedent to OnSpot's obligation to begin performing Services.

In the event Client fails to remit payment of any invoice by the due date, OnSpot reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to draw against the security deposit to satisfy any outstanding fees and accrued interest. Upon such draw, Client shall replenish the security deposit to its full original amount within five (5) business days of written notice from OnSpot. Failure to replenish the deposit within the required period shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement.

In the event Client terminates this Agreement prior to the expiration of the Initial Term or any Renewal Term without cause, the security deposit shall be forfeited in full and retained by OnSpot as liquidated damages, and not as a penalty, reflecting the reasonable cost of redeployment and lost revenue. If the Agreement runs its full term and all invoices are paid in full, the deposit will be applied as a credit against the final invoice.

2.4 Invoices. OnSpot shall invoice the Client on the 1st day of each month for the fees incurred by the Client in that respective period (the “Invoice”). Invoices sent monthly cover services from the 1st to the last day of the prior month.

2.5 Payment Remittance. The Client shall pay all undisputed fees set forth in the Invoice immediately upon receipt of the Invoice.

2.6 Delayed Fees. In the event that undisputed fees are not paid within ten (10) calendar days after the date of the Invoice, the total amount of such unpaid undisputed fees shall be considered “Delayed,” and without affecting any of OnSpot’s other rights or remedies, shall be subject to monthly compounding interest at a rate

of three percent (3%) per month from the Invoice date until paid in full.

2.7 Suspension of Services. Failure to submit payment for fees within fifteen (15) calendar days after the date of the Invoice shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement. Under this material breach, OnSpot reserves the right to immediately suspend any and all Services to Client, at its sole discretion, with written notice, until all outstanding fees and accrued interest have been paid in full. Suspension of Services does not relieve the Client of its payment obligations under this Agreement.

2.8 Delinquent Fees. In the event that undisputed fees are not paid within thirty (30) calendar days after the date of the Invoice, the total amount of such unpaid undisputed fees shall be considered “Delinquent.” OnSpot reserves the right to pursue all available legal remedies for collection of Delinquent fees, including reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs of collection.

3. Staffing Fees

3.1 Staffing. In the performance of the Services, OnSpot shall utilize certain staff members, in accordance with the Job Titles and Billable Rates set forth and detailed in the applicable Statement of Work.

3.2 Onboarding Period. OnSpot shall develop the necessary infrastructure related to the Services (“Onboarding”), as further described in the Statement of Work. During the Onboarding period, the Client may incur additional fees solely as agreed upon by both Parties. The Client will incur fees for staff at the rates listed in the applicable Statement of Work if the Onboarding is unreasonably extended due to Client’s inability to provide the necessary information to perform the Services, provided OnSpot gives prior written notice that such fees may be incurred.

3.3 Work Days & Rest Days. Services for each OnSpot staff member shall be scheduled in a four (4) consecutive hour block per day, which includes one (1) fifteen-minute break. Total of twenty (20) billable hours per week. Break times will be staggered to allow for continuous coverage by OnSpot staff members for Client on each of five (5) days per seven (7) consecutive day period beginning on each Sunday (the “Work Week”). Each day, comprising four (4) billable hours, shall be known as a “Work Day.” Days that are not Work Days shall be known as “Rest Days.”

3.4 Personal Days. In the event an assigned OnSpot staff member does not perform Services on any given scheduled Work Day due to illness, injury, or another personal reason, OnSpot will make its best efforts to replace such member with an alternate OnSpot staff member of equal competency and skill level. For the avoidance of doubt, Client will not incur billable fees attributable to an OnSpot staff member’s missed scheduled Work Days where that staff member is not replaced by an alternate OnSpot staff member of equal competency and skill level. Adjustments on the billable are based on 22 workdays per month.

3.5 Holidays. OnSpot does not observe or designate any company holidays, although staff members may specifically request to observe a holiday as a personal day subject to client approval. The Client will not incur any cost for any holiday taken. If a holiday is taken, resulting in the Client receiving less than the expected work days per month, OnSpot will compensate the Client by offering additional Work Days in lieu of the holiday, or alternatively will adjust the billable fees in accordance with Section 3.4.

3.6 Overtime Hours. The Client may request in writing that OnSpot staff members render “Overtime Hours,” defined as all scheduled hours beyond four (4) hours in any given Work Day, or any hours worked during Rest Days. The rate for Overtime Hours for an OnSpot staff member shall be equal to one and one-half (1.5) times the applicable hourly rate for such staff members as set forth in the Statement of Work. For the avoidance of

doubt, Overtime Hours will only be due where the Client has explicitly requested Overtime Hours in writing and, prior to the Overtime being undertaken, has agreed in writing to the additional cost.

3.7 Staffing Levels. The Client may not reduce the number of hours below the “Minimum OnSpot Staff” number set forth in the applicable Statement of Work until the next Renewal Term (defined below), without the agreement of OnSpot. However, the Client may request an increase in the number of staff members by submitting its written request to OnSpot at least thirty (30) calendar days before the additional staff members are to begin performing Services, and OnSpot shall make its best reasonable efforts to fulfill Client’s request within that notice period. The increase shall only become effective upon an executed Change Order as described in Section 1.2, and receipt of any applicable Set-Up Fee within fifteen (15) days of the date of the executed Change Order.

3.8 Renewal Rate Increase. Each staff member’s billable rate shall increase by no more than three percent (3%) per Renewal Term (defined below).

4. Term & Termination

4.1 Initial Term. This Agreement will begin on the Effective Date and continue for a period of one (1) year (the “Initial Term”) from the “Program Launch Date” as identified in the attached Statement of Work, unless otherwise extended or earlier terminated in accordance with the provisions set forth below.

4.2 Renewal. After the Initial Term, the Agreement shall be subject to renewal for successive one (1) year periods (each, a “Renewal Term”), subject to Section 3.8 (“Renewal Rate Increase”), unless either Party provides written notice to the other of its intent not to renew at least thirty (30) calendar days prior to the end of the Term then in effect. OnSpot will notify the Client at least ninety (90) calendar days prior to any Renewal Term automatically coming into effect. The Initial Term and any Renewal Terms are collectively referred to as the “Term.”

4.3 Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate this Agreement at any time for cause if (i) the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) calendar days of receiving written notice of such breach, or (ii) the other Party ceases its operation, dissolves or commences any bankruptcy, receivership, or other procedure for the relief from creditors.

4.4 Break Clause. From the Effective Date, the parties will enter a 30-day trial period. During this trial period, either Party may terminate this Agreement without penalty, having given fourteen (14) days written notice.

4.5 Termination Date & Effect of Termination. The last date of the Term of this Agreement, having been terminated or allowed to expire pursuant to the terms above, shall be the “Termination Date.” Upon the Termination Date, each Party shall promptly deliver to the other any property of the other in its possession or under its control, including any and all Confidential Information (defined below) of the other pursuant to this Agreement; and all fees that have accrued prior to the Termination Date shall become immediately due and payable upon the Termination Date.

5. Confidential Information.

5.1 Defined. “Confidential Information” includes, without limitation, information relating in any way to either Party’s business models, policies, procedures, requirements, practices, intellectual property, trade secrets, systems, strategies, techniques, technology, sales presentation, Client’s customer data, pricing and cost information, marketing plans, forecasts, software, systems, infrastructure, or processes whether obtained

before or after the Effective Date, or other information of a similar nature, not generally disclosed to the public, including but not limited to, any information designated by either Party as confidential.

5.2 Exceptions. The obligations imposed by this Section shall not apply to any Confidential Information that (i) is proven to have been lawfully received from a third party without accompanying use or disclosure restrictions; (ii) is proven to have been independently developed by a Party’s employees and/or agents; (iii) becomes publicly known without breach of this Agreement by a Party or its employees and/or agents; (iv) is approved for release in writing by an authorized representative of the disclosing Party; or (v) is required to be disclosed pursuant to direct order of a court of competent jurisdiction, duly authorized subpoena, or governmental authority, provided that the responding Party gives sufficient notice to the disclosing Party to enable the disclosing Party to take protective measures, and in any event only discloses the exact Confidential Information, or portion thereof, specifically requested.

5.3 Obligations. Each Party in receipt of Confidential Information of the disclosing Party agrees: (i) to maintain in strict confidence all such Confidential Information by using at least the same level of care that it uses for its own confidential information, but in no case less than a prudent and reasonable standard of care; (ii) not to disclose any such Confidential Information without the prior express written consent of the disclosing Party, except to its employees and/or agents on a need-to-know basis and who are under an obligation of confidentiality at least as strict as in this Section 5; (iii) not to use such Confidential Information for any purpose other than that for which it is disclosed under this Agreement.

5.4 Return of Confidential Information. Upon the written request of the disclosing Party, or promptly upon termination of this Agreement, the receiving Party shall return, or certify that it has destroyed, all Confidential Information disclosed under this Agreement and any and all documents or files, whether paper, computer, electronic, or otherwise, containing such Confidential Information of the disclosing Party.

5.5 Injunctive Relief to Protect Confidential Information. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Agreement, each Party acknowledges that monetary remedies may be inadequate to protect Confidential Information and that injunctive relief may be sought to protect such Confidential Information.

6. Intellectual Property

6.1 Deliverables. Subject to Client’s payment obligations and OnSpot’s retained rights in OnSpot Property (defined below), Client shall own all rights, title and interest in any deliverable or outcome resulting from the performance of Services created by OnSpot for Client (the “Deliverables”) during the Term of the Agreement. OnSpot hereby assigns all rights, title and interest in the Deliverables to the Client. OnSpot agrees, at Client’s reasonable expense, to execute any documents and take any actions reasonably requested by Client to perfect or maintain Client’s ownership of the Deliverables.

6.2 OnSpot Property. Notwithstanding Section 6.1, OnSpot shall retain all rights, title and interest in its materials, ideas, concepts, know-how, techniques, processes, technology and other intellectual property (“OnSpot Property”), including any OnSpot Property utilized, created, developed or conceived by OnSpot in connection with the performance of the Services that are not specific to Client, do not contain Client Confidential Information, and are of general use, even if incorporated into the Deliverables. OnSpot shall be free to use the OnSpot Property and its general knowledge, skills and experience on other engagements. Subject to the Client’s satisfaction in fulfilling its payment obligations hereunder, OnSpot hereby grants to the Client a perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use any OnSpot Property included as part of the Deliverables.

7. Non - Solicitation

7.1 Client agrees that during the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months following the termination of this Agreement, it will not knowingly solicit for employment any employee or independent contractor of the Company who performed Services under this Agreement. An individual’s response to a broad and general advertisement or solicitation not specifically targeting or intending to target employees of OnSpot shall not be deemed a violation of this Section 7.1. If the Client breaches this section, in addition to any other remedies OnSpot may have at law or in equity, OnSpot will be entitled to a payment from Client equal to USD 10,000.

8. Indemnification

8.1 General. Each Party (the “Indemnifying Party”) agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other Party, its directors, officers, employees, parents, Affiliates, agents, successors and assigns (collectively, the “Indemnified Party”), against any and all liabilities, losses, damages (excluding special, incidental, or consequential damages), claims, causes of action and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses, arising directly or indirectly, as a result of (a) any physical damage or injury to body or tangible personal property sustained by the Indemnified Party to the extent caused by the gross negligence or willful misconduct of the Indemnifying Party in connection with this Agreement; (b) any employment related claim by an employee, agent, or contractor of the Indemnifying Party arising from or based on their employer-employee relationship, including but not limited to claims for benefits, unpaid wages, worker’s compensation, or wrongful termination; (c) any third party claim arising from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of the Indemnifying Party; or (d) any claims or expenses resulting from the Indemnifying Party’s disregard of or failure to abide by the applicable laws or regulations controlling or specific to the operation of its business and with respect to the collection, use, protection, disclosure, retention and disclosure of personal information.

8.2 Infringement Claims. OnSpot agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client, its directors, officers, and employees against any and all liabilities, losses, damages, claims, causes of action and expenses, arising out of or relating to an action against Client brought by a third party to the extent that the action is based upon a claim that any Services or Deliverables infringe upon or misappropriate a patent, trademark, or copyright of such third party. In the event any Deliverable becomes, or in OnSpot’s opinion is likely to become, the subject of a claim that it infringes any third party’s intellectual property rights, OnSpot may, at its option and expense, either (i) procure for Client the right to continue using the Deliverable, (ii) replace or modify the Deliverable so that it becomes non-infringing, or (iii) accept return of the Deliverable and give Client a refund of the fees paid by Client for the Deliverable. THIS SECTION STATES ONSPOT’S ENTIRE LIABILITY AND CLIENT’S SOLE AND EXCLUSIVE REMEDY FOR INFRINGEMENT CLAIMS AND ACTIONS.

8.3 Process. The foregoing obligations are conditioned on the Indemnified Party (i) notifying the Indemnifying Party promptly in writing of such action, (ii) giving the Indemnifying Party sole control of the defense thereof and any related settlement negotiations, and (iii) cooperating and, at the Indemnifying Party’s request and expense, assisting in such defense or settlement.

9. Warranties/Disclaimer of Warranties/Limitation of Liability

9.1 OnSpot represents and warrants that (i) OnSpot has the full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder; and (ii) the Services shall be provided in a timely and professional manner consistent with industry standards, and in accordance with all applicable laws, rules, and

regulations of the United States and any other applicable country, state or jurisdiction.

EXCEPT AS PROVIDED HEREIN, ONSPOT DISCLAIMS ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE AND NONINFRINGEMENT, AND ANY IMPLIED WARRANTIES ARISING FROM STATUTE, COURSE OF DEALING, COURSE OF PERFORMANCE, OR USAGE OF TRADE.

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER OF THE PARTIES BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES FOR LOST PROFITS OR LOST DATA OR OTHERWISE, EVEN IF THE PARTIES HAVE BEEN MADE AWARE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY’S TOTAL CUMULATIVE LIABILITY FOR ANY DAMAGES OR LOSS FOR ALL CLAIMS ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT, THE USE OF OR INABILITY TO USE THE DELIVERABLES OR ANY SERVICES PROVIDED HEREUNDER, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF ACTION, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, EXCEED THE FEES PAID BY CLIENT FOR THE SERVICES DURING THE TWELVE MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE DATE THE CLAIM AROSE OR UP TO $1,000,000 IF SUCH CLAIM INCLUDES LOSS OR BREACH OF CLIENT DATA. THE LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 9.1 SHALL NOT APPLY TO (i) ONSPOT’S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, (ii) BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY UNDER SECTION 5 OF THIS AGREEMENT, OR (iii) EITHER PARTY’S WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE.

10. Arbitration

10.1 Except as set forth in Section 2 with respect to the recovery by OnSpot of collection amounts, the Parties agree that any claim, controversy or dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement or any SOW (each, a “Dispute”) shall be resolved, to the fullest extent permitted by law, by final, binding and confidential arbitration before a single arbitrator selected from and administered by the State of New York. The arbitration shall take place in New York. Both Parties agree to share equally the fees of the arbitrator and the costs of arbitration; however, each Party shall be responsible for its own attorneys’ fees, costs and disbursements. The arbitrator shall not have the authority to modify any provision of this Agreement or to award punitive damages. The decision rendered by the arbitrator will be final and binding on the Parties.

11. General Provisions

11.1 Labor & Compliance. Both Parties affirm that each shall comply in all material respects with all laws, rules, and regulations applicable to each Party’s business and services in each jurisdiction where its operations may take place throughout the Term of this Agreement.

11.2 Assignment and Affiliates. Neither Party may assign its rights or delegate its obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. OnSpot may assign its rights and obligations under this Agreement to a parent or subsidiary or to a successor, whether by way of merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties to this Agreement and their respective successors and assigns. The Client recognizes that OnSpot’s Affiliates may provide Services under this Agreement. Each Party shall be responsible for its Affiliates’ compliance with this Agreement and for any breach of this Agreement by any of its Affiliates. Whenever used in this Agreement, the term “Affiliates” means with respect to any person or entity, all persons or entities directly or indirectly through one or more

intermediaries (i) controlled by the person or entity, (ii) that control the person or entity, or (iii) that are under common control with the person or entity, and all directors, managers, members, shareholders, officers, and partners of any such entity.

11.3 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of New York, without reference to principles of choice of law. Any action or proceeding seeking to enforce any provision of, or based on or arising out of, this Agreement shall be brought in the state and federal courts of the State of New York.

11.4 Force Majeure. The parties hereto shall not be responsible for any failure or delay in the performance of any obligations hereunder to the extent caused by acts of God or the public enemy, flood, fire, natural disaster, war or preclusive acts of any governmental authority, provided that performance will be excused only to the extent of, and during the disability, and the Party takes reasonable measures to remove the disability.

11.5 Notices. Any notice, request, demand or other communication required or permitted hereunder shall be in writing, shall reference this Agreement and shall be either: (a) delivered by hand; (b) sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or (c) sent by an express courier, with written confirmation of receipt.

TO: ONSPOT TECHNOLOGIES INC. {{onspot.address}} Email: nur@onspotglobal.com Email cc: legal@onspotglobal.com

11.6 Severability. If any term, provision, covenant or condition of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, void or unenforceable, the rest of the Agreement shall remain in full force and effect, and shall in no way be affected, impaired or invalidated.

11.7 Relationship of Parties. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as creating an agency, partnership, joint venture or any other form of association, for tax purposes or otherwise, between the Parties; and the Parties shall always be and remain independent contractors.

11.8 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, including all exhibits or appendices, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and supersedes and replaces all prior and contemporaneous understandings or agreements, written or oral, regarding such subject matter. No amendment or modification of this Agreement will be binding unless in writing and signed by a duly authorized representative of both parties.

11.9 Survival. In addition to any rights that accrued prior to termination, the provisions of Sections 5 through 11 shall survive any termination of this Agreement until the obligations or time limitations of those sections are completed.

11.10 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed simultaneously in one or more counterparts, each of which will be deemed an original, but all of which together will constitute one and the same instrument.

11.11 Authority, Consent & Approvals. Any individual signing this Agreement on behalf of an entity hereby represents and warrants in his or her individual capacity that he has full authority to do so on behalf of that entity. A Party shall not unreasonably withhold or delay giving a consent provided for in this Agreement unless the Agreement specifically permits otherwise.

APPENDIX A

STATEMENT OF WORK

This Statement of Work (“SOW”) is entered into by and between {{onspot.entityName}} (“OnSpot”) and {{client.legalEntityName}} (“Client”). This SOW will be effective as of {{offer.startDate}} (“Effective Date”).

This SOW is entered into pursuant to and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of, that certain Master Service Agreement dated {{contract.effectiveDate}} between OnSpot and Client (the “Agreement”). Capitalized terms contained in this SOW shall have the meaning ascribed to them in the Agreement, unless otherwise expressly defined in this SOW. In the event of a conflict between the terms of this SOW and the Agreement, the terms of the Agreement shall govern unless expressly provided otherwise in this SOW.

1. Scope of Work

OnSpot will provide the following services to the Client under this Agreement:

OnSpot provides staff to the client that shall perform the tasks and responsibilities indicated in the Job Description attached herewith. The staff deployed to the client shall be on an exclusive basis and shall not be deployed to a competitor or similar industry services within the {{contract.serviceArea}} area within 6 months after a tenure with the Client. Furthermore, OnSpot guarantees that the staff chosen by the Client to perform duties indicated in the Job Description attached herewith is a dedicated resource. No other OnSpot staff shall be allowed to perform such duties unless otherwise approved by the client.

2. Staffing Fees & Billable Rates

To render the Services, OnSpot shall deploy {{contract.numberOfFte}} that will cover the required hours of the Client as stipulated in this Agreement.

In accordance with Sections 2 and 3 of the Agreement, fees shall be incurred by Client for all activities related to the performance of Services based on the Minimum Number of Hours, Billable Rates, and commission rate listed below:

Security Deposit: Client shall provide a security deposit equal to one (1) month's total invoice amount upon execution of this Agreement. This deposit will be applied as a credit against the final invoice upon successful completion of the Agreement, provided all prior invoices are paid in full.

Minimum Hours Required per week: {{contract.minimumWeeklyHours}} HOURS/Week Cost per FTE: {{offer.rate}} Total Monthly Recurring Charge: {{contract.monthlyRecurringCost}} Security Deposit: {{deposit.amount}}

3. Onboarding Period

The Parties contemplate that immediately following the Effective Date, OnSpot shall develop the necessary infrastructure related to the Services (“Onboarding”). The Parties anticipate that the Onboarding will last

approximately 2 weeks. The Client will be responsible for providing reasonably related documentation, system access, and other necessary information to perform the Services as reasonably requested by OnSpot during Onboarding. The client will incur all costs in connection with the training of OnSpot staff at the billable rates identified above during Onboarding.

4. Hours of Operation

Subject to the provisions set forth in the Agreement, the Services shall be performed during the hours specified by the Client and may be modified in a subsequent Change Order, signed by both Parties.

5. Actions Affecting Personnel

Except as expressly set forth herein, OnSpot shall retain the sole and exclusive control over its employees and independent contractors for purposes of performing the Services, including but not limited to the recruitment, hiring, performance management or termination of personnel, or any other employee-related action, throughout the Term.

6. Location of Operation

The Services shall be rendered using OnSpot or its Affiliate employees and independent contractors located in the Philippines or any other country in which OnSpot or its Affiliates may have operations, with certain administrative and managerial support located in the United States.

7. Provided Equipment & Software

OnSpot performs the Services with the following standard set-up:

Standard Equipment PC, monitor, mouse, keyboard, headset, and webcam (available upon request with additional charges)

Standard Software: G Suite, Chrome, Mozilla, Opera, Adobe Air, Acrobat, Shockwave, and VLC Player. The Client may request additional equipment and software so long as the Client agrees to incur all reasonable costs in connection with such a request.
